text:
miguel: hey everyone, day 3 rookie question. installed Homebrew on my M1 (so /opt/homebrew), used asdf for node/python, and rustup for Rust. `cargo install cargo-edit` succeeds but binaries end up in /Users/miguel/.cargo/bin which isnt in PATH for GUI apps (VS Code actions fail). Also sometimes `rustc` from brew shows up instead of rustup. how do folks standardize Rust tooling with asdf + brew on macos-arm?

lara: welcome! common pattern: use rustup (recommended) and ensure CARGO_HOME and RUSTUP_HOME are in your dotfiles before other PATH changes. example in ~/.zprofile or ~/.zshenv: 
```
export CARGO_HOME="$HOME/.cargo"
export RUSTUP_HOME="$HOME/.rustup"
export PATH="$CARGO_HOME/bin:$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"
```
put that early so GUI apps launched from Spotlight/VS Code get it.

miguel: ah i had asdf lines after brew stuff. i also have a brew rust from `brew install rust` that added /opt/homebrew/bin earlier in PATH. should i uninstall brew rust?

sam: i'd remove brew rust to avoid clashes. rustup manages toolchains and `rustc + stable --version` etc. If you keep brew rust you can get mismatched cargo/rustc combos. `brew uninstall rust` and then `rustup default stable` is clean.

lara: also check `which rustc` and `type -a rustc cargo` after you update PATH. If `~/.cargo/bin/rustc` appears, good. If `brew` still shows up, `hash -r` or restart the shell.

miguel: did `brew uninstall rust` and added the exports to ~/.zprofile above. restarted mac, `which cargo` now shows ~/.cargo/bin/cargo. VS Code terminals still reported old PATH when run from the Dock. launching code from terminal (`code .`) fixes it, but want a permanent fix for GUI launches.

devx: for mac GUI apps you need environment variables exported in login shells. ~/.zprofile is run for login shells. If you use zsh and open apps from the Dock, macOS runs a login session that reads ~/.zprofile, but sometimes Spotlight uses launch services which don't. Best practice: put minimal CARGO_HOME/RUSTUP_HOME exports in ~/.zprofile and restart the OS or log out/in so launchd picks them up. Also we keep a short note in the onboarding doc about this.

miguel: noted. one extra weirdness: when i `cargo install` a tool it sometimes overwrites a binary that brew previously installed (like `exa`). how to prefer cargo-installed bins?

sam: that's simply PATH order. ensure `$CARGO_HOME/bin` is earlier than `/opt/homebrew/bin` if you prefer cargo binaries first. But be deliberate: some brew-installed utils are patched/have different behavior. We usually put `CARGO_HOME/bin:$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH` so dev-installed tools take precedence for developer workflow.

lara: tiny tip: add a dotfile comment like `# Developer tools wins: put .cargo and asdf shims first` so future hires know order matters. Also run `env | grep -E "CARGO_HOME|RUSTUP_HOME|PATH"` and paste when troubleshooting.

miguel: thanks folks. i moved the exports to ~/.zprofile, uninstalled brew rust, reordered PATH to put cargo first, restarted, and `which exa` now points to ~/.cargo/bin/exa. opened a PR to the onboarding doc with the snippet and a short explanation. :tada:

devx-bot: Welcome @miguel! Awesome write-up. If you include the exact snippet and a brief "why" in the PR we'll fold it into the central dev-setup doc. :sparkles:
